articles.title: Kevin McGonigle Was Confused by His Curtain Call
articles.summary: Kevin McGonigle got a curtain call in the Tigers finale and had no idea it was coming. #Tigers
articles.body:
The Detroit Tigers were trailing 4-0 in the bottom of the seventh inning against the Pittsburgh Pirates in the final game of the 2026 MLB season on Sunday. Kevin McGonigle hit a solo home run to left-center, and it turned out to be his last at-bat of the year.

In the top of the eighth inning, manager A.J. Hinch pulled McGonigle after the rookie had already taken the field at third base. McGonigle pointed to himself and asked, "Me?" Then came the standing ovation from the Comerica Park crowd. The 22-year-old played 156 games for Detroit in 2026 and was one of the few bright spots in a 76-86 season.

Kevin McGonigle Speaks Out About Being Pulled

McGonigle talked to Jason Beck of MLB.com after the game about the eighth-inning move. "I was more confused. I didn't expect that. It was really cool," he said.

A Rookie Season Among the Best Since 1947

McGonigle finished with a .278 batting average, 18 home runs and 72 RBIs, plus 12 stolen bases in 16 attempts. He posted a .376 on-base percentage, a .430 slugging percentage and an .806 OPS. He entered Sunday leading all American League position players in bWAR , not just rookies, and his 6.9 mark would be the eighth highest by a rookie since the Rookie of the Year Award debuted in 1947. He could well win the American League award this year.

A.J. Hinch Was Going to Pull Him in the Seventh Inning

Hinch had planned to take McGonigle out after his seventh-inning at-bat and had a pinch-runner ready to go. The home run foiled that. Hinch told Beck:

"I think we found the one thing we get to talk to Kevin about improving over the winter, which is the curtain call." "I thought he was going to single or walk or double or something. And then he goes ahead and hits a homer." "Respecting what that accomplishment is matters to me. So I wanted to at least get him a chance to get an ovation in front of our home fans. I probably should've gone to the mound and actually told him what I was doing, but it gave the boys on the bench some ammo to get under Kevin's skin."

"I thought he was going to single or walk or double or something. And then he goes ahead and hits a homer."

"Respecting what that accomplishment is matters to me. So I wanted to at least get him a chance to get an ovation in front of our home fans. I probably should've gone to the mound and actually told him what I was doing, but it gave the boys on the bench some ammo to get under Kevin's skin."

Hinch also called it an "incredible season, and a fitting way for him to cap it with some good at-bats today and the opposite-field homer." The Tigers missed the postseason, but McGonigle gave them plenty to build on heading into 2027.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy is rare company in NFL history after trade to the Giants
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy joins other former top picks in NFL history after his trade.
articles.body:
The long-awaited news that Vikings fans had been hearing rumors of since the preseason dropped on Monday around lunchtime.

It came down from The Ringer's Tom Pelissero when he reported that the team was trading away J.J. McCarthy . The Vikings were trading him to the New York Giants in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick, which shows that the value of the former top pick has fallen off over the years since being drafted.

ESPN's Kevin Seifert added a wrinkle to the trade news. He shared some information from the Elias Sports Bureau. Seifert explained, "J.J. McCarthy is 1 of 4 first-round QBs in the past 25 years to start 10 or fewer games for the team that drafted them."

The other three quarterbacks are not the company someone hopes to make when they are a top draft pick. They were:

Not the greatst company to have but as Trey Lance has shown he bounced back and has hung around the NFL. McCarthy may have a chance to start for the Giants this seaosn due to Jaxson Dart being out and Jameis Winston not playing as well as they had hoped. All is not lost for him but there examples pointing to it may be.

articles.title: How the mighty have fallen: Steph Curry reacts to Warriors expectations
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry is back healthy. He was shocked to hear expectations placed on the Warriors.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO ― The Golden State Warriors will only go as far as their franchise leader Stephen Curry will take them.

That is partially why it was important for him to ink a deal to return to the Warriors for the next year or two. Now that the dust has settled and the ink is dry, an area of focus for Curry will be his availability.

Curry missed 39 games for the Warriors last year with knee issues. Entering his 18th season, he's not getting any younger. He spent the offseason nursing his knee through many rounds of golf during the summer, now he's ready for basketball.

"Knee is feeling great, ready to go. No issues at all. There is a management element of it for sure where you just have to be mindful of everything that you're doing in practice, games, preparation," Curry said. "We haven't talked about the game schedule yet or anything like that where I'm kind of getting too far ahead of myself, but for training camp and the preseason schedule and getting myself into shape and ready to go, there's no limitations at all."

Curry is more confident going into the year, he said, after becoming stronger and understanding that he doesn't have 18-year-old knees anymore, let alone 28-year-old ligaments.

"So I'm excited to get out there and hoop. I feel like I've built a really good foundation over the summer to be in a much better position up until, what, November last year, it wasn't really any kind of signs or symptoms, but I feel a lot stronger and more understanding of what I'm dealing with," he said. "That gives me a lot of confidence going into the year."

articles.title: White Sox Wild Card Series: Watch Schedule And TV Details
articles.summary: Chicago White Sox fans can watch the Wild Card Series against Houston on NBCSN and Peacock. Get the full schedule, times, and broadcast info here.
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox have punched their ticket to the postseason, but the path to glory starts with a tricky viewing puzzle. The team faces the Houston Astros in a best-of-three Wild Card Series that kicks off on Tuesday, September 29. All games will take place at Daikin Park in Houston, meaning the White Sox must win on the road to advance. Fans across the country need to know exactly where to look to catch the action, as the broadcast setup is more complex than a standard regular-season game.

Most fans will need a streaming subscription to watch the White Sox play. NBCSN will broadcast the initial two contests while Peacock offers live streaming, as reported by Yahoo Sports . NBCSN is a cable channel that does not have widespread carriage anymore, so many viewers will miss the game on their standard TV packages. Per South Side Sox , the only local option for color commentary is Steve Stone, who will join the Peacock broadcast to provide analysis. This means a Peacock subscription is the most reliable way for fans to follow the team, with plans starting at $12.99 a month.

The schedule is tight and follows a specific pattern for all four Wild Card matchups. Game 1 is set for 4 p.m. CT on Tuesday, followed by Game 2 at the same time on Wednesday. If the series goes to a deciding third game, it will happen on Thursday, October 1. The start time for Game 3 depends on when the other series conclude, per the schedule released by NBC Sports . Fans must check their streaming apps or cable guides closely, as the time could shift to 1 p.m. or 7 p.m. CT based on the results of the Phillies , Cubs , and Red Sox games.

NBC has brought in a strong team to call the action for this series. The broadcast features play-by-play announcer Tom McCarthy, who is known for calling Philadelphia Phillies games. Geoff Blum and Steve Stone, representing the Astros and White Sox respectively, will accompany him as analysts. Per NBC Sports, former pitcher Adam Ottavino will serve as the "Inside the Pitch" analyst, while field reporter Britney Eurton will provide updates from the dugout. This setup ensures fans get deep insights from former players who know the teams well.

There is a catch for those who prefer traditional cable over streaming. NBCSN returned in late 2025 but is only carried on a few services like Xfinity, YouTube TV, and Fubo, according to Yahoo Sports. If a fan does not have one of these specific providers, they cannot watch on TV and must use Peacock. This split in the broadcast rights means some fans might be left out if they do not have the right subscription. The network is trying to balance its cable and streaming platforms, but it creates a hurdle for the average viewer trying to tune in.

Playing the entire series in Houston is a significant disadvantage for the White Sox. Per South Side Sox, the compressed playoff schedule leaves no room for a travel day, forcing the lower seed to play all three potential games in the opponent's stadium. This setup tests the team's mental toughness and ability to perform under pressure without home-field support.

The stakes are high for a team that has struggled to find consistency in recent years. Every pitch matters when the series is short and played entirely on the road. If the White Sox can overcome the odds and the difficult viewing setup for fans, they could advance to the Division Series. The Division Series begins on Saturday, October 3, giving the team very little time to rest or prepare if they win. The path to the World Series starts here in Houston, and the fans watching from home will need to be ready for a grueling battle.
